indicator.name: Buildings in areas impacted by wildfire
indicator.definition: Context for building exposure to historical burned areas. Exposure intersections, confirmed damage and future risk are distinct measures.

records.title: Portugal study shows building-data choice changes WUI delineation
records.summary: A mainland Portugal comparison evaluates official residential records, Microsoft building footprints and World Settlement Footprint for wildland–urban interface mapping. Results differ substantially across input frames.
records.why_relevant: Supports explicit building-source selection and denominator checks before interpreting 6.1.1. WUI delineation is a related exposure context.
supporting_passages: only 46% of the total WUI area being identified by all three datasets

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.
The reported comparison concerns WUI area and building datasets, not a national 6.1.1 exposure value or confirmed damage. The study’s historical fire perimeters cover 2000–2023.

key_statistics.statistic_text: WUI area identified by all three compared building datasets
key_statistics.measure: WUI area identified by all three compared building datasets
key_statistics.source_quote: only 46% of the total WUI area being identified by all three datasets

records.title: GABAM v3 publishes annual burned-area maps for 2014–2024
records.summary: The dataset authors release Landsat-derived annual burned-area maps as geographic tiles at 0.00025-degree spacing, described as approximately 30 metres. Version v3 includes a GABAM2024 archive.
records.when_happened: Version v3 published 17 December 2025; annual coverage 2014–2024
records.who_published: Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences · Zenodo
records.why_relevant: A directly relevant candidate burned-area source for 6.1.1. The inspected publication documents the product; raster bytes were not downloaded or validated in this intake.
records.publisher: Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences · Zenodo

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.
Angular grid spacing varies in ground distance with latitude. Burned pixels do not alone establish wildfire attribution, building damage, future probability or observation completeness.

records.title: GHS-OBAT R2024A: a candidate building frame with mixed data vintages
records.summary: JRC’s building attribute table supplies country-grouped records, centroid coordinates and identifiers linked to Overture’s July 2024 release, with building characteristics derived from GHSL data.
records.when_happened: Issued 16 December 2024; 2020 reference attributes and 2024 Overture identifiers
records.why_relevant: Directly relevant to the building-record frame used in 6.1.1’s current research card. Metadata and representative points require checks before spatial overlay.
supporting_passages: unique identifiers to link to Overture buildings 2024-07-22.0

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.

Release label, geometry source vintage and reference-year attributes differ. Dataset documentation does not establish complete national building coverage, authenticate local files or provide burned-area exposure results.

records.title: Camp Fire case: temporary refuge areas as an evacuation contingency
records.summary: NIST researchers reconstructed evacuation during the 2018 Camp Fire in Butte County. Their case study reports outcomes from improvised temporary refuge areas when evacuation routes became unsafe.
records.when_happened: Camp Fire, November 2018; study published August 2026
records.who_published: NIST · Eric Link and Alexander Maranghides
records.why_relevant: Shows a documented adaptation response in fire-affected communities and the practical need to locate exposed settlements.

case_study.intervention: Temporary fire refuge areas as evacuation contingencies.
case_study.implementation: Ad hoc refuges were used when fire blocked evacuation routes.
case_study.result: The authors attribute saved lives and reduced exposure to the temporary refuges.
case_study.measurable_result: 31 refuge areas; at least 261 civilian lives saved, as reported by the study.
case_study.usefulness: A documented contingency for evacuation planning in fire-affected communities.
evidence_quotes: The ad hoc use of 31 temporary refuge areas saved at least 261 civilian lives

supporting_passages: The ad hoc use of 31 temporary refuge areas saved at least 261 civilian lives
records.publisher: NIST · Eric Link and Alexander Maranghides

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.

This retrospective evacuation case concerns people’s safety. Its author-attributed outcomes are not a controlled estimate of intervention effectiveness and do not measure buildings intersecting burned areas.

records.title: EU wildfire strategy links prevention and preparedness to spatial planning
records.summary: The Commission’s integrated wildfire approach covers prevention, preparedness, response and recovery. Its proposals include incorporating prevention and preparedness into spatial planning.
records.why_relevant: Supplies policy context for why planning authorities need building-exposure evidence and improved fire monitoring.
supporting_passages: proposing EU countries integrate wildfire prevention and preparedness into spatial planning

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.
This source describes a Commission strategy and proposed actions. It does not establish a mandatory building code or demonstrate implementation outcomes.

records.title: EFFIS records 1,079,538 hectares burned in the EU in 2025
records.summary: JRC reports that the EU’s 2025 burned area was the largest in the EFFIS record since 2006. The release accompanies an advance regional fire-season assessment.
records.why_relevant: A documented annual burned-area context and candidate hazard source for 6.1.1; building intersections still require separate calculation.

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.
This is EU27 land area mapped as burned, not the number or percentage of buildings affected. The wider Europe, Middle East and North Africa total uses a different geographic denominator.

records.title: US study projects rising structural losses under a no-adaptation scenario
records.summary: This study combines burned area, settlement patterns and structural vulnerability to project US fire losses through 2060 under business-as-usual conditions without adaptation.
records.why_relevant: Provides a trend framework connecting fire hazard and the built environment. Its projected losses are separate from 6.1.1’s historical burned-area intersections.
supporting_passages: 133,200–449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century.

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.
Modelled damage or destruction is conditional on the study’s scenario and assumptions. It is not an observed building-exposure count, a global estimate or a validated Forge measurement.

key_statistics.statistic_text: Projected cumulative damaged or destroyed structures under business-as-usual conditions without adaptation
key_statistics.measure: Projected cumulative damaged or destroyed structures under business-as-usual conditions without adaptation
key_statistics.source_quote: 133,200–449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century.

records.title: EU wildfire update: burned area remains above the long-term average
records.summary: JRC’s dated EFFIS update compares the 2026 fire season with 2025 and the 2006–2025 baseline. It provides mapped fire activity for prioritising further investigation.
records.when_happened: Situation as of 7 October 2026; page updated 8 October 2026
records.why_relevant: A recent hazard footprint context for 6.1.1; building records must be intersected separately to measure building exposure.
supporting_passages: the area affected by fires has reached 692 419 hectares.

validation_warnings.message: Public-source preview snapshot. Human review is pending.

The figures cover land area, not buildings. EFFIS maps fires around 30 hectares or larger and can include intentional vegetation-management burns. The page reports conditions on 7 October and an update on 8 October 2026; its original publication date is unknown.

warnings: Bounded public-source preview; not an exhaustive search or a shared review workspace.
